business_problem: dsm-firmenich needed a more proactive way to identify and predict mycotoxin contamination in feed crops because contamination threatens food safety, animal health, regulatory compliance, and agricultural economics across a large global customer base.
solution_summary: Researchers at dsm-firmenich Animal Nutrition & Health used IBM Environmental Intelligence Suite to build a predictive mycotoxin-risk service that combines global weather, geospatial, crop, fungal, and occurrence data. The system analyzes hourly weather observations and forecasts extending up to eight months across 61,000 locations, then feeds those conditions into algorithms that account for crop growth stages, fungal life cycles, mycotoxin biochemistry, and historical occurrence data to estimate contamination risk in wheat, corn, soybeans, and other crops. dsm-firmenich also feeds survey and detection-service data back into the models so the forecasts can be refined and tied to recommended mitigation strategies such as earlier testing, altered harvest timing, fungicides, binders, or enzymatic biotransformation. Because the model can produce both regional and farm-specific forecasts, the company turned environmental intelligence into a field-level risk-management workflow that helps partners decide where to monitor more closely and how to reduce loss before contaminated feed enters the supply chain.

solution_components.name: IBM Environmental Intelligence Suite
solution_components.role: Supplies global weather, forecast, API, analytics, and geospatial inputs for the mycotoxin prediction models.

solution_components.name: Mycotoxin prediction
solution_components.role: Represents the dsm-firmenich predictive service that turns weather and occurrence data into actionable contamination-risk forecasts.

data_flow: Hourly weather observations and long-range forecasts from Environmental Intelligence Suite are combined with crop, fungal, and historical mycotoxin occurrence data, scored by prediction algorithms, and returned as regional or farm-level risk forecasts that guide testing, harvesting, and mitigation decisions.
business_outcome: The service helps feed producers and growers spot contamination risk earlier, target monitoring and mitigation more precisely, reduce crop loss and chemical overuse, and protect food and feed quality with more trustworthy forecasts.

Farm-level predictions are tailored using local factors such as soil tillage, previous crops, and development timing.
Survey results feed back into the model to refine predictions and mitigation guidance.
